Higher baseline Fibromyalgia Survey Questionnaire scores in RA patients independently predicted higher DAS28-CRP disease activity 12 weeks after DMARD initiation or change.
The Widespread Pain Index component of the FSQ was significantly associated with increased follow-up DAS28-CRP scores in RA patients.
The Symptom Severity Scale component of the FSQ was not significantly associated with follow-up DAS28-CRP scores in RA patients.
Females had a higher observed rate of long COVID diagnosis compared to males in the unmatched study population.
Pre-existing chronic lung disease (including asthma, COPD, emphysema, and bronchiectasis) was associated with higher odds of subsequent long COVID diagnosis in the matched cohort.
Pre-existing renal disease was associated with higher odds of long COVID diagnosis in the matched cohort.
Pre-existing migraine was significantly more common among patients who subsequently developed long COVID compared to matched controls.
Pre-existing fibromyalgia was significantly more common among patients who subsequently developed long COVID compared to matched controls.
Patients who developed long COVID were significantly more likely to be hospitalized within 14 days of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection than matched controls.
Patients who developed long COVID had significantly higher ICU admission rates during acute infection compared to matched controls.
During acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, patients who later developed long COVID had a higher neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio than matched controls.
Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) was elevated during acute infection in patients who subsequently developed long COVID compared to matched controls.
Serum triglyceride levels were substantially elevated during acute infection in patients who subsequently developed long COVID compared to matched controls.
Serum HDL cholesterol levels were lower during acute infection in patients who subsequently developed long COVID compared to matched controls.

Antivirals, anticoagulants, and steroids were administered at significantly higher rates in the long COVID cohort than in matched controls during acute and post-acute phases, consistent with more severe acute disease.
Albuterol administration was already elevated in the long COVID cohort during the baseline (pre-infection) phase, consistent with a higher prevalence of chronic pulmonary disease in this group.
Monoclonal antibody administration did not differ significantly between the long COVID and control cohorts.
Unlike most tracked phenotypes, brain fog and sleep problems increased in reported frequency from the acute to the post-COVID-19 phase in the long COVID cohort.
Cough, difficulty breathing, and tiredness were the most commonly reported new-onset phenotypes among long COVID patients during the post-COVID-19 phase.

Both the long COVID and control cohorts showed elevated serum glucose during the acute COVID-19 phase, suggesting acute metabolic dysfunction common to SARS-CoV-2 infection rather than a distinguishing marker for long COVID.
Pediatric patients with generalized joint hypermobility had significantly higher mean and median bleeding scores than healthy pediatric controls.
Among patients with generalized joint hypermobility, higher Beighton scores (a measure of joint hypermobility severity) were not correlated with higher bleeding scores.
Three-quarters of patients with generalized joint hypermobility had an abnormal bleeding score, indicating a high burden of clinically relevant bleeding symptoms in this population.
The most commonly reported bleeding symptoms among patients with generalized joint hypermobility were oral bleeding, easy bruising, and bleeding with minor wounds.
Despite a high prevalence of abnormal bleeding scores, only a small minority of patients with generalized joint hypermobility had previously been evaluated by hematology for bleeding symptoms.
A preconception history of migraine was not appreciably associated with risk of spontaneous abortion.
Migraine frequency (number of episodes in the 4 weeks before baseline) was not appreciably associated with SAB risk across all frequency categories.
Migraineurs who reported no preconception migraine medication use did not have a higher risk of spontaneous abortion than non-migraineurs.
Migraineurs who used migraine medication in the 4 weeks before conception had a slightly higher risk of spontaneous abortion compared with non-migraineurs.
Daily use of migraine medication was associated with an increased risk of spontaneous abortion.
Less than daily use of migraine medication was not associated with increased risk of spontaneous abortion.

Use of prescription migraine prophylaxis medication, indicative of more severe migraine, was associated with the greatest increase in spontaneous abortion risk of any subgroup, though based on very few exposed cases.
Use of prescription (episodic) migraine treatment medication was not appreciably associated with spontaneous abortion risk.
Use of over-the-counter episodic migraine medication showed a modest, non-significant increase in spontaneous abortion risk.
Use of combination analgesic/caffeine medication for migraine was associated with a borderline increased risk of spontaneous abortion.
Triptan use was associated with a modestly increased, non-significant risk of spontaneous abortion, to a lesser extent than reported in a prior study.

The association between migraine medication use and spontaneous abortion was similar across most exposure-timing windows but was strongest when medication use was assessed more than 8 weeks before conception.
Use of pain medication for indications other than migraine was not associated with spontaneous abortion risk.
Use of pain medication specifically for migraine was associated with a modest, non-significant increase in spontaneous abortion risk.
Use of aspirin for migraine was associated with a slight increased risk of spontaneous abortion compared with no pain medication use.
Use of aspirin for indications other than migraine was associated with a decreased risk of spontaneous abortion compared with no pain medication use.
Use of non-aspirin NSAIDs showed no meaningful association with spontaneous abortion risk.
Participants with migraine were more likely than those without migraine to report a history of infertility and diagnoses of PCOS, endometriosis, or anxiety disorders, regardless of medication use.
Migraineurs who took medication for migraine had a higher prevalence of prior history of spontaneous abortion at baseline than migraineurs without medication use or non-migraineurs.
Participants with the COL5A1 rs12722 CC genotype showed a significantly lower (reduced) average external tibial rotation of the non-dominant knee compared with the combined TT/CT genotype group.

None of the individually tested COL5A1, COL11A1 or COL11A2 genotypes showed significant effects on general participant characteristics, flexibility training, Beighton score or sit-and-reach range of motion.
A higher combined collagen 'protective' genotype score (COL5A1/COL11A1/COL11A2) was associated with higher active genu recurvatum angle values, indicating less knee hyperextension.
A higher combined collagen genotype score was also associated with higher passive genu recurvatum angle values (less hyperextension).
There was a significant positive correlation between an increasing collagen genotype score and increasing active genu recurvatum angle (less hyperextension).
There was a significant positive correlation between an increasing collagen genotype score and increasing passive genu recurvatum angle (less hyperextension).
The combined collagen genotype score had no significant effect on any anterior-posterior tibial translation or external-internal tibial rotation measurements of the non-dominant knee.

In multiple linear regression, the collagen genotype score together with age, sex and body mass significantly predicted passive genu recurvatum, with the full model explaining 18% of variance compared to 15% without genotype.
Unlike for passive genu recurvatum, the collagen genotype score was not a significant predictor of active genu recurvatum in the regression model.
There were no significant differences in computed absolute length changes of the knee-stabilising ligaments (ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL bundles) between collagen genotype score groups.

A greater proportion of participants with the lowest (0) collagen genotype score were able to hyperextend their non-dominant knee beyond 10 degrees on the Beighton test compared to those with higher genotype scores.

The combined genotype score also had no significant effect on general characteristics, flexibility training, Beighton score, or sit-and-reach measurements, whether analysed in the full cohort or the RKT sub-cohort.
Visual dependence, assessed via the rod and frame test, was present in 83% of the vestibular migraine group.
Individuals with vestibular migraine exhibited significantly lower baseline electrodermal activity than healthy participants.
Vestibular migraine patients showed significantly greater normalized vertical trunk acceleration than healthy participants during postural challenge with visual conflict.
Vestibular migraine patients showed significantly greater normalized medial trunk acceleration than healthy participants.
In the vestibular migraine group, tonic EDA activity increased significantly over the course of the trial.
Vertical trunk acceleration was significantly associated with EDA, Dizziness Handicap Inventory scores, and Activities-specific Balance Confidence scores.
In healthy adults, higher tonic EDA activity was associated with more accurate postural reactions.

Several RCTs found that low-frequency heart rate variability in migraine patients was significantly reduced during electroacupuncture at Fengchi (GB20) and Shuaigu (GB8), suggesting the antimigraine effect of acupuncture involves ANS regulation.
IBS patients show increased sympathetic nervous system activity compared with healthy controls.
IBS patients show decreased parasympathetic nervous system activity compared with healthy controls.
Patients with cervical and shoulder pain and fibromyalgia exhibit excessive sympathetic activity together with reduced parasympathetic activity.

Patients with functional dyspepsia show increased sympathetic tone and decreased vagal reactivity on 24-hour HRV monitoring, and those with autonomic dysfunction report more severe indigestion symptoms.

Reactive astrocytes in the medial thalamic nucleus and anterior cingulate cortex contribute to visceral hypersensitivity in an IBS model, and electroacupuncture at ST25 and ST37 alleviates this hypersensitivity by reducing astrocyte activation in these regions.

P2X3 receptors in the prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex mediate visceral pain in IBS, and electroacupuncture at ST37 and ST25 reduces visceral pain sensitivity by downregulating P2X3 receptor expression in these regions.
Electroacupuncture at ST36 reduces visceral hyperfunction in IBS by downregulating serotonin (5-HT) neuronal activity in the brainstem and spinal cord.

Mice with inflammatory bowel disease show elevated P2Y12 receptor expression in the prefrontal cortex accompanying visceral pain and depression, and electroacupuncture at Dachangshu (BL25) downregulates P2Y12, attenuates microglial activation and IL-1β expression, reducing both visceral pain and depressive symptoms.

Percutaneous electrical stimulation at ST36 reduces the cumulative incidence of post-stroke constipation, increases spontaneous defecations, and is accompanied by increased vagal nerve activity and reduced sympathetic nerve activity.

In an RCT for functional constipation, electroacupuncture at ST25, Fujie (SP14), and Shangjuxu (ST37) increased the number of entirely spontaneous defecations while decreasing the prevalence of adverse effects, though whether these effects relate to ANS regulation remains unclear.
Acute CPAP at increasing levels (4-16 cm H2O) produced a dose-dependent decrease in systolic blood pressure in supine, awake patients with autonomic failure and supine hypertension.
The CPAP-induced fall in systolic blood pressure was attributable in part to a reduction in stroke volume.
CPAP acutely reduced cardiac output alongside the drop in blood pressure.
Systemic vascular resistance did not change significantly during acute CPAP administration.
Heart rate did not change significantly during acute CPAP administration.
Overnight CPAP therapy lowered nighttime systolic blood pressure compared with placebo in a crossover trial of 11 patients with autonomic failure.
Overnight CPAP reduced nighttime urine output compared with placebo in patients with autonomic failure and supine hypertension.
Overnight CPAP therapy improved morning orthostatic tolerance, measured as the area under the blood pressure curve during standing, compared with placebo.
The authors conclude that CPAP represents a novel nonpharmacologic treatment for supine hypertension in autonomic failure that also improves nocturia and daytime orthostatic hypotension.
Women with migraine showed lower total frequency-domain variance of heart rate variability compared to age-matched controls.
The migraine group showed reduced vagal (parasympathetic) autonomic influence, evidenced by a lower HF band power compared to controls.
The migraine group showed a decrease in sympathetic autonomic influence, evidenced by a lower LF band power compared to controls.
Time-domain heart rate variability analysis showed decreased vagal modulation, expressed by lower SD, in women with migraine compared to controls, with a large effect size.
RMSSD, a time-domain marker of vagal modulation, was significantly decreased in women with migraine compared to controls, with a large effect size.
Normalized LF and HF units and the LF/HF ratio (sympathovagal balance) did not differ significantly between the migraine and control groups.
Blood pressure variability, including variance and absolute LF power, did not differ between women with migraine and controls.
Total baroreflex gain was significantly decreased in women with migraine compared to controls.
Baroreflex gain down was significantly decreased in women with migraine compared to controls.
Baroreflex gain up was significantly decreased in women with migraine compared to controls.
Women with migraine had significantly higher pain catastrophizing scores compared to controls.
Women with migraine had significantly higher Central Sensitization Inventory scores compared to controls.
Women with migraine had significantly higher Beck Depression Inventory scores compared to controls.
Plasma metabolomic profiling showed that phosphocholine and ceramide lipids were the dominant components distinguishing the metabolite profile of fibromyalgia patients from healthy controls.

In the soreness-dominant fibromyalgia subgroup, plasma sphingomyelin (d18:1/18:0) and ceramide (C18:1/C22:1) concentrations were elevated compared to healthy controls, whereas no such elevation was seen in the pain-dominant subgroup.
In a mouse model of stress-induced fibromyalgia-like hyperalgesia, several lipid classes—lysophosphatidylcholines, phosphatidylcholines, sphingomyelins and ceramides—were upregulated.
Treatment with darapladib and antioxidants inhibited LPC16:0 synthesis and alleviated stress-induced hyperalgesia in the fibromyalgia mouse model.
Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1P1) signaling through immune and epithelial cells may modulate autoimmune phenotypes in primary Sjögren's syndrome.
A case-control study found differences in the lipidomic profiles of tears and saliva between primary Sjögren's syndrome patients and healthy controls, with 29 of 86 individual lipid species altered.

In an animal model of primary Sjögren's syndrome, anti-ceramide treatment with myriocin decreased interferon-γ expression and Th1 cell frequency, suppressed salivary gland inflammatory infiltration, and maintained salivary flow rate.
Greater BMP6 expression was observed in the salivary glands of 54% of a cohort of primary Sjögren's syndrome patients, and this correlated with a lower unstimulated whole saliva flow rate.
In a mouse model, inhibiting BMP6 signaling reduced SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation in the submandibular glands, decreased inflammation, and restored salivary gland function.

S1P promotes cell survival and proliferation, whereas ceramides and sphingosine inhibit proliferation and stimulate apoptosis, a balance relevant to immune and epithelial cell regulation in primary Sjögren's syndrome.
A founder splice-site mutation in ELP1, enriched in Ashkenazi Jews due to a historical genetic bottleneck, causes impaired ELP1 splicing and Familial dysautonomia.
FD patients, homozygous for the mutant ELP1 allele, show tissue-specific reductions in Elp1 protein primarily in the nervous system.
FD patients exhibit reduced BMI, elevated metabolic rate, and low body fat content indicative of metabolic dysfunction.
Alpha-diversity of the stool microbiome was significantly lower in FD patients compared to paired healthy relatives.
FD patients had significantly fewer bacterial taxa (OTU richness) than their paired relatives, averaging 45 fewer taxa.
FD patients were significantly more likely to cluster into microbiome enterotype 1, while relatives were associated with enterotype 2.
The FD-associated enterotype (cluster 1) exhibited significantly lower alpha diversity than the relative-associated enterotype (cluster 2).
The health-associated bacterial genus Faecalibacterium (OTU 4) was significantly less abundant among FD patients compared to relatives.
The health-associated bacterial genus Roseburia (OTU 9) was significantly less abundant among FD patients compared to relatives.

FD relatives' gut microbiome diversity was not significantly different from that of healthy individuals in independent published cohorts, whereas FD patients' microbiomes were the most divergent of all groups compared.
FD patients had significantly lower serum xanthine levels than their relatives.
FD patients had significantly lower serum methanol levels than their relatives.
FD patients had significantly elevated serum urea levels compared to relatives, consistent with clinical BUN measures.
FD patients had significantly elevated stool choline levels compared to relatives, the only significant difference among 73 stool metabolites measured.
Among FD patients, higher stool choline levels significantly correlated with lower microbiome alpha diversity, decreased richness, and fewer OTUs shared with relatives.

FD patients who used a gastrostomy tube (G-tube) exclusively (no oral feeding) had less diverse gut microbiomes, shared fewer OTUs with relatives, and were nearly 5 times more likely to have the FD-associated microbiome enterotype than patients still eating orally.
FD patients treated with antibiotics within three months prior to sampling were more than four times as likely to have the FD-associated dysbiotic gut microbiome enterotype than untreated patients.
Fundoplication surgery to reduce acid reflux was significantly associated with stool choline levels in FD patients.
Sex, weight, and BMI were evaluated as potential covariates of gut microbiome and metabolome diversity in FD patients but none reached statistical significance.

Serum creatinine levels were positively correlated with microbiome beta-diversity distance between FD patients and relatives, and negatively correlated with the proportion of shared OTUs between pairs.
Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was positively correlated with microbiome richness, number of OTUs shared with relatives, and number of unique OTUs in FD patients.
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels were positively correlated with the proportion of OTUs shared between FD patient-relative pairs.
Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) from clinical chemistry panels correlated significantly with serum urea measured by NMR metabolomics, serving as an internal validation of the metabolomics approach.

Among all clinical and demographic factors evaluated, patient age was the strongest correlate of gut microbiome diversity, being positively associated with microbiome variability and beta-diversity distance from relatives, and negatively associated with the number of OTUs shared with relatives.
In a neuronal Elp1-deletion mouse model of FD, gut microbiome diversity began diverging from littermate controls as early as 14 days post-weaning when mice were housed separately by genotype.
By 54 days post-weaning, FD mice housed separately from controls showed significantly greater dispersion (variability) in gut microbiome composition than control mice.
Stool metabolome profiles (68 metabolites) became significantly divergent between FD mice and control mice by 162 days post-weaning.

Cohousing FD mice with control littermates (allowing coprophagy-mediated microbiome homogenization) eliminated significant microbiome and metabolome differences between genotypes at the 79 DPW timepoint, whereas separately housed FD and control mice showed significant divergence at that same age.

Cohousing FD mice with control littermates significantly lowered disease pathology scores (body condition, hind limb clasping, kyphosis) compared to FD mice housed separately, across multiple age ranges.
Gut transit time, which was significantly slower in separately housed FD mice compared to controls, was significantly increased (improved) when FD mice were cohoused with control littermates.

Separately housed FD mice had elevated stool choline at the final 279 DPW timepoint and elevated levels of the choline-derived metabolite methylamine at 179 and 279 DPW compared to the same mice when cohoused with controls, mirroring altered choline metabolism seen in human FD patients.

Comparison of FD relatives' gut microbiomes with those of unrelated healthy subjects from two independent published studies found little evidence that the ELP1 founder mutation carrier status meaningfully alters microbiome diversity, whereas FD patients' microbiomes remained the most distinct of all cohorts compared.
Fibromyalgia, diagnosed by modified 2010 ACR criteria, was present in 6.0% of Chinese hospital patients with primary headache.
Primary headache patients with comorbid fibromyalgia were older on average than those without fibromyalgia.
Women were more likely than men to have comorbid fibromyalgia among primary headache patients.
Patients with headache and fibromyalgia had lower educational attainment than those without fibromyalgia.
Headache duration was longer in patients with comorbid fibromyalgia than in those without.
Depression was substantially more prevalent in headache patients with comorbid fibromyalgia than in those without.
Anxiety was more prevalent among primary headache patients with comorbid fibromyalgia than those without.
Insomnia was substantially more common among primary headache patients with comorbid fibromyalgia than those without.
Fibromyalgia was more prevalent among patients with chronic migraine than those with episodic migraine.
Fibromyalgia was more prevalent among patients with chronic tension-type headache than those with episodic tension-type headache.
The majority of fibromyalgia-related pain in this cohort localized to the shoulders, neck, and upper back.
Patients with Parkinson disease had lower nerve fiber densities (intraepidermal, sudomotor, and pilomotor) than patients with multiple system atrophy.
Phosphorylated alpha-synuclein was detected in skin biopsies of all patients with multiple system atrophy and most patients with Parkinson disease, but not in healthy controls.
Patients with multiple system atrophy showed greater cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein deposition than patients with Parkinson disease.
Multiple system atrophy patients had a more widespread peripheral distribution of cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein than Parkinson disease patients.

Combined measurement of phosphorylated alpha-synuclein deposition and distribution in skin biopsy distinguished multiple system atrophy from Parkinson disease with greater than 90% sensitivity and specificity.
Five patients presented with overlapping clinical features of both migraine and cluster headache, making differential diagnosis difficult.
The authors note that migraine and cluster headache differ in headache frequency, duration, and inter-attack (inter-bout) pathophysiology, though shared pathways may exist between them.

Each of the five patients underwent thorough examination to exclude secondary causes of headache and had trialed multiple medications, implying prior treatment attempts were unsuccessful or inconclusive given the diagnostic ambiguity.
Changes in baseline systolic blood pressure at late phase 2 of the Valsalva maneuver were lower in late-onset dOH patients compared with controls.
The heart rate difference between baseline and Valsalva phase 3 (ΔHR) was lower in late-onset dOH patients than in controls.
The Valsalva ratio was lower in late-onset dOH patients compared with controls.
Pressure recovery time (PRT) at Valsalva phase 4 was longer in late-onset dOH patients than in controls.
The differences in PRT and ΔHR between late-onset dOH patients and controls remained statistically significant after adjusting for age.
A PRT cutoff of ≥2.14 seconds combined with ΔHR ≤15 bpm distinguished late-onset dOH patients from age- and sex-matched controls.
Longer PRT was associated with increased likelihood of having late-onset dOH.

A pressure recovery time cutoff of 2.14 seconds or longer combined with a heart rate change of 15 bpm or less distinguished late-onset delayed orthostatic hypotension patients from age- and sex-matched controls.
Longer pressure recovery time increased the likelihood that a patient had late-onset delayed orthostatic hypotension.
A smaller heart rate change between baseline and phase 3 of the Valsalva maneuver increased the likelihood that a patient had late-onset delayed orthostatic hypotension.
Longer pressure recovery time was associated with a greater likelihood of having early-onset rather than late-onset delayed orthostatic hypotension.
Diabetic obese (BKS-db/db) mice showed approximately 30% lower hepatic and renal serine levels than wild-type mice.
Glycine levels were reduced by 30-50% in liver, kidney, inguinal white adipose tissue and plasma of db/db mice relative to wild-type controls.
Methionine, linked to serine via one-carbon metabolism, was also reduced in liver, adipose tissue and plasma of db/db mice.
Hepatic serine dehydratase (Sds) expression was significantly upregulated in db/db mice, consistent with increased serine catabolism.
Hepatic serine hydroxymethyltransferase 1 (Shmt1) expression was upregulated in db/db mice.
Hepatic Shmt2 expression was upregulated in db/db mice.
Hepatic 10-formyltetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase (Aldh1l1) expression was upregulated in db/db mice.
Glycine decarboxylase (Gldc), a component of the glycine cleavage system, was increased in db/db liver.
Dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase (Dld) expression was increased in db/db liver.
3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (Phgdh), a de novo serine synthesis enzyme, was significantly reduced in db/db liver.
Methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase 2 (Mthfd2) expression was significantly reduced in db/db liver.
db/db diabetic mice showed a significant reduction in serine tolerance test (STT) AUC despite receiving a higher glucose+serine dose, indicating elevated postprandial serine disposal.

STZ-induced insulin-deficient diabetic mice also showed elevated serine disposal after combined glucose/serine challenge relative to vehicle controls, indicating insulin deficiency alone can drive the phenotype.

Fourteen-week-old db/db diabetic mice exhibited thermal and tactile hypoalgesia along with decreased motor nerve conduction velocity, indicating peripheral neuropathy coincident with impaired serine homeostasis.
Serine- and glycine-free diets effectively reduced circulating and hepatic serine and glycine in the fed state (but not fasted state) in mice fed low-fat or high-fat backgrounds.
Dietary serine and glycine restriction attenuated high-fat-diet-induced weight gain without altering food, calorie or water intake or physical activity.
Despite attenuating obesity, mice on the serine/glycine-restricted high-fat diet remained glucose and insulin intolerant, showing that reduced adiposity did not correct glucose/insulin dysregulation.
Dietary serine and glycine restriction potently reduced hepatic de novo palmitate synthesis by approximately 70% relative to serine-replete diets.

Hepatic protein expression of ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY), acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC2) and stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD1) were each reduced by approximately 50% with dietary serine restriction, while cholesterol biosynthesis enzymes were unchanged or increased.

Long-term (12-month) feeding of a serine- and glycine-free diet caused progressive thermal hypoalgesia and reduced intraepidermal nerve fibre density in paw skin, a clinical marker of small sensory fibre degeneration.

Combining serine/glycine restriction with a high-fat diet accelerated the onset of peripheral neuropathy, producing marked thermal hypoalgesia after only three months compared with the 12 months needed on a chow-based serine-free diet.
High-fat feeding reduced faecal microbial alpha diversity, whereas serine/glycine restriction increased alpha diversity in the low-fat diet context but not in the high-fat context.
Serine and glycine restriction in the high-fat diet reduced the proportion of gut microbial strains possessing a complete fatty acid synthesis pathway.
Hepatic de novo cholesterol synthesis was increased in mice fed a serine/glycine-restricted high-fat diet compared with high-fat diet alone.

Changes in AKT phosphorylation at Ser473 and Thr308 tracked with dietary fat and carbohydrate content rather than with serine/glycine levels, suggesting serine restriction affects lipid metabolism independent of insulin signalling.
Myriocin treatment attenuated HFD-induced weight gain without changing plasma serine and glycine levels.
Myriocin treatment protected corneal small-fibre nerve density in mice fed the serine/glycine-restricted high-fat diet.
Dietary serine/glycine restriction did not change the respiratory exchange ratio, indicating no shift in systemic substrate utilization between carbohydrate and lipid oxidation.
One week after streptozotocin treatment, plasma glycine and branched-chain amino acids were altered, but plasma serine was not yet changed, in insulin-deficient mice.
db/db mice showed increased circulating 1-deoxysphinganine as well as increased hepatic ceramides and deoxydihydroceramides.
Myriocin dosing for eight weeks increased intraepidermal nerve fibre density in db/db mice.

Myriocin did not affect body weight gain, hyperglycaemia, or plasma serine levels in db/db mice, but strongly reduced canonical sphingolipids in the liver with limited effects on paw skin 1-deoxysphingolipids and ceramides.
Both heavy bupivacaine-dextrose prolotherapy (HDP) and autologous blood injection (ABI) produced a successful outcome in the majority of patients with chronic painful TMJ sub-luxation.
Both treatment groups showed a statistically significant reduction in recorded pain score along with reduced maximum inter-incisal opening (MIO) after treatment.
Neither HDP nor ABI injection produced any morphological changes to the mandibular condyle on imaging.

The authors conclude HDP is a safe and simple modality with predictable clinical outcomes for symptomatic chronic TMJ sub-luxation, offering combined local anaesthetic and proliferant delivery in a single injection.
At baseline, the GJH group had a significantly higher Beighton score than the non-GJH group, consistent with the group definition criteria.
After balance training, the GJH group showed significantly greater improvement in FAAM-Sport scores than the non-GJH group at post-training and 3 months post-training.
The re-sprain ratio after balance training was lower in the GJH group than in the non-GJH group at both post-training and 3 months post-training.
FAAM-ADL scores improved over time in both groups after balance training with no significant difference between GJH and non-GJH groups.
Before training, the GJH group had significantly worse dynamic postural stability than the non-GJH group in the posterolateral and posteromedial reach directions.
After balance training, both GJH and non-GJH groups showed similar improvements in dynamic (SEBT) and static (BES) postural control measures.
At baseline, there were no significant differences in isokinetic ankle muscle strength between the GJH and non-GJH groups.
Balance training produced differential strength gains between groups, with significant group x time interactions for dorsiflexion and plantarflexion strength, generally favoring the GJH group.
After balance training, the GJH group showed a sustained increase in 60°/s dorsiflexion strength while the non-GJH group's initial increase reverted to baseline.
At 3 months post-training, the GJH group had a significant increase in 120°/s dorsiflexion strength, while the non-GJH group remained at baseline level.
The GJH group had a greater increase in 60°/s plantarflexion strength than the non-GJH group at both post-training and 3 months post-training.

Overall, CAI patients with generalized joint hypermobility achieved equivalent or better clinical outcomes than those without GJH after a 12-week balance training program, suggesting balance training remains a viable conservative option before surgery is considered.
Among 500 adults with epilepsy, 163 (32.6%) reported experiencing headache on at least one day per month.
Migraine was the most frequent primary headache type in epilepsy patients, affecting 54 of 163 headache patients (33.1%), of whom 41 had migraine without aura and 13 with aura.
Tension-type headache was equally common as migraine among epilepsy patients with headache, affecting 54 of 163 patients (33.1%).
Trigeminal autonomic cephalgia (e.g. cluster headache) was reported by 7 of 163 headache patients (4.3%), a rare but notable subgroup.
One in five epilepsy patients with headache (20.2%) did not meet full ICHD-3 criteria for any single primary headache type and were classified as non-classifiable headache.
Chronic headache (≥15 days/month) occurred in 15 of 163 patients (9.2%), comprising 7 chronic migraine, 5 chronic tension-type headache, and 3 chronic trigeminal autonomic cephalgia cases.
Headache was significantly more prevalent among female than male epilepsy patients (108 vs 55 of the 163 headache patients).
Among female epilepsy patients with headache, 37.0% met criteria for migraine (29 without aura, 11 with aura).
Among male epilepsy patients with headache, 25.5% met criteria for migraine (12 without aura, 2 with aura).
The relative distribution of headache subtypes (migraine, TTH, TAC) did not differ significantly between female and male epilepsy patients.
The type of epilepsy (focal, generalised, unclassifiable) was not significantly associated with the distribution of primary headache types.

Epilepsy patients on antiepileptic drug (AED) monotherapy reported migraine less frequently than those on polytherapy, with no such difference for tension-type headache or trigeminal autonomic cephalgia.
Of the 163 epilepsy patients with headache, 66 (40.5%) reported headache temporally associated with seizures (pre-, ictal, or post-ictal).
Among seizure-associated headaches, isolated postictal headache was the most common presentation, reported in 30 patients, compared with 8 with isolated preictal and 2 with isolated ictal headache.
Patients with headache were disproportionately more likely to not achieve seizure freedom, though the association only reached borderline significance.
Migraine prevalence among epilepsy patients (roughly one-third) was higher than the reported prevalence of migraine in the general population (10.0%).

Trigeminal autonomic cephalgia prevalence in this epilepsy cohort was higher than lifetime prevalence rates reported in general-population epidemiological studies, possibly reflecting shared trigeminovascular, autonomic, hypothalamic and vagal pathophysiology, or seizure-driven activation of trigeminovascular neurons.
Tension-type headache prevalence in this epilepsy cohort was lower than reported in the general adult population, but comparable to prior epilepsy-specific studies.
Chronic headache prevalence in the epilepsy cohort (9.2%) was slightly higher than reported in the general population (4.8%).
No patients with generalised epilepsy reported trigeminal autonomic cephalgia, whereas this rare headache type occurred mostly in patients with focal epilepsy.
Vagal tone is reported to be low in many chronic pain patients and related to how long they have had pain.
Heart rate variability has been shown to improve following even milder exercise programs similar to the one proposed in this study.
Elevated basal C-reactive protein is associated with both the presence and severity of chronic low back pain even after adjusting for confounders such as obesity.
Elevated basal interleukin-6 is associated with both the presence and severity of chronic low back pain even after adjusting for confounders such as obesity.
Exercise exerts anti-inflammatory effects and has been shown to substantially decrease levels of inflammation.
A prior study using the same self-administered acupressure mHealth app reduced low back pain by 35% compared with usual care.
The same mHealth acupressure app produced significant improvements in pain, fatigue, sleep, and depression among 288 fatigued breast cancer survivors.
In a small unpublished pilot of cLBP patients treated with acupuncture, greater baseline widespread pain was significantly associated with better subsequent acupuncture response.
A cited study (Witt et al.) found that females were more likely than males to respond to acupuncture, a pattern seen with treatments that act primarily through the central nervous system.
Baseline pressure pain thresholds were differentially predictive of response to verum versus sham acupuncture, with patients having higher pain thresholds more likely to respond to verum acupuncture.
Reduction in posterior insula glutamate following acupuncture was significantly correlated with reduction in chronic pain among nociplastic pain patients.
Reductions in insula-to-default mode network connectivity following acupuncture were correlated with improvements in clinical pain in a nociplastic pain population.

After a 4-week MBSR course, cLBP patients showed significantly increased activity in the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, regions implicated in descending pain inhibition.

In healthy volunteers, mindfulness training was associated with increased activity in sgACC, orbitofrontal cortex, and insula, and decreased activity in the primary somatosensory cortex and thalamus during evoked pain.
Meta-analyses report that mindfulness-based interventions reduce pain intensity and pain interference across chronic pain syndromes, including cLBP, with effect sizes of 0.3-0.5.
Neuropathic pain patients with diminished endogenous pain inhibition, as measured by conditioned pain modulation, were more likely to respond to duloxetine.

Milnacipran (an SNRI) preferentially worked in individuals with decreased connectivity between the periaqueductal gray and insular cortex, and between the rostral anterior cingulate cortex and insular cortex, consistent with decreased descending analgesia.

The stimulated inflammatory response after LPS-stimulation is strongly associated with nociplastic pain characteristics such as multifocal pain and the number of pain syndromes present, as shown in the MAPP study.

Arterial stiffness (PWV) also showed a U-shaped pattern across quartiles of orthostatic systolic blood pressure reaction, being highest with the most extreme BP increase or decrease.
The occurrence of carotid plaque differed significantly across quartiles of orthostatic systolic BP reaction, while diabetes prevalence did not.
An exaggerated orthostatic BP increase correlated with higher BMI and waist circumference.
Greater height was associated with a more pronounced orthostatic systolic BP decrease.
Coronary artery calcification score did not differ significantly across quartiles of resting heart rate.
Higher resting heart rate was significantly associated with greater arterial stiffness (PWV), along with age, blood pressure, and anthropometric measures.
Higher resting heart rate was associated with a worse metabolic/inflammatory profile, including elevated CRP, triglycerides, glucose and HbA1c, and lower HDL cholesterol.
Resting heart rate was not significantly associated with pulse pressure or LDL cholesterol.
Use of antihypertensive drug treatment was more common among individuals with higher resting heart rate.
Diabetes mellitus prevalence was higher among individuals with higher resting heart rate.
Smoking status did not differ significantly according to resting heart rate quartiles.
Coronary artery calcification score was positively associated with arterial stiffness (PWV) in the population.

Patients with biallelic loss-of-function variants in IPO8 display a highly consistent phenotype resembling Loeys-Dietz syndrome, including early-onset thoracic aortic aneurysm and connective tissue findings such as arachnodactyly and joint hypermobility, along with facial dysmorphisms, high arched or cleft palate/bifid uvula, and motor developmental delay.

An induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line (BBANTWi011-A) was generated from PBMCs of a patient homozygous for the IPO8 c.1420C>T (p.Arg474*) variant, and the resulting iPSCs expressed pluripotency markers and could differentiate into all three germ layers.
Prior studies have shown that eptinezumab reduces the burden of migraine on patients as early as one day after administration.

An exploratory subgroup analysis of the PROMISE-2 trial found that eptinezumab reduced monthly migraine days by 2.0 days more than placebo in patients with chronic migraine and medication-overuse headache.
In the DEFINE3 study, combining preventive treatment with medication withdrawal reduced monthly migraine days by 1.7 and 1.4 more than withdrawal alone at 2 and 4 months, respectively.

Medication overuse occurs in up to 50% of individuals with chronic migraine and triggers medication-overuse headache in about 60 million people, making MOH one of the top 20 causes of disability worldwide.
Brief Educational Intervention (BEI) has demonstrated long-term efficacy in reducing medication overuse in patients with medication-overuse headache and is safe, effective, and low-cost.
Patients with a dual diagnosis of chronic migraine and medication-overuse headache have a greater disease-based burden than patients with chronic migraine alone.
Eptinezumab has high bioavailability and reaches maximum plasma concentration within 30 minutes of intravenous administration.
Autonomic dysfunction was reported in 19.1% of the 68 patients with thymoma-associated autoimmune encephalitis.
Autonomic nervous dysfunction was significantly more frequent in patients with poor prognosis than those with good prognosis after treatment for thymoma-associated autoimmune encephalitis.
Sleep disturbances were significantly more common in the poor prognosis group and did not appear to benefit from treatment.
Mental/psychiatric disorders were significantly more common in patients with poor prognosis compared to those with good prognosis.
Anti-Ma2 antibody positivity was significantly associated with poor prognosis in thymoma-associated autoimmune encephalitis.
Lack of timely thymoma intervention (surgery, radiotherapy, or chemotherapy) was significantly associated with poor prognosis.
The majority of patients (79.7%) showed symptomatic improvement after first-line immunotherapy and/or thymoma intervention.
Anti-AMPAR antibodies were the most frequently detected autoantibody in patients with thymoma-associated autoimmune encephalitis.
Anti-CRMP5 (CV2) antibody was the third most common antibody detected and this patient group was noted to be vulnerable to myasthenia gravis with relatively poor clinical prognosis.
Anti-LGI1 antibody positivity in this thymoma cohort (8/58) was higher than the ~10% tumor-association prevalence reported previously, suggesting possible selection bias.

Anti-AChR antibody was strongly associated with thymoma-associated autoimmune encephalitis patients, consistent with the known high prevalence of AChR antibodies in myasthenia gravis patients with thymoma.
Utilization of gamma globulin (IVIG) treatment was significantly higher in male patients than female patients.
MRI abnormalities were found in 81.0% of patients, predominantly involving the hippocampus and temporal lobe, with some cortical/subcortical involvement.
Abnormal EEG findings, mostly frontotemporal slow and sharp wave activity, were present in 69.8% of patients, including some without clinical seizures.
Relapse occurred in 14.8% of patients during follow-up.
Fibromyalgia (ACR-FMS score ≥13) was associated with significantly increased odds of strongly agreeing that pain was a major reason for continued opioid use (pain-related OUD maintenance).
Fibromyalgia was associated with significantly increased odds of strongly agreeing with needing ever-increasing opioid doses to control pain (pain-related OUD escalation).
Identifying as White race was independently associated with increased odds of endorsing pain-related OUD escalation within the same regression model.
Fibromyalgia was associated with significantly increased odds of strongly agreeing with delaying OUD treatment due to fear of worsened pain during opioid abstinence.
Fibromyalgia was associated with significantly increased odds of strongly agreeing with fear of future pain-precipitated relapse.

In hierarchical regression, fibromyalgia predicted higher total Pain-related OUD Exacerbation Scale (PrOUD ES) scores after controlling for gender, race, OUD severity, opioid type, mental health, and pain severity.
The newly developed 4-item PrOUD ES demonstrated a single-factor structure explaining 70.39% of variance and high internal consistency (Cronbach alpha 0.859).
PrOUD ES scores were positively correlated with the number of painful body regions reported, supporting construct validity.
Lower (worse) RAND-36 Bodily Pain quality-of-life scores were correlated with greater PrOUD ES scores, further supporting construct validity.

Among 125 individuals with pain and OUD, 39 (31.2%) met ACR-FMS survey criteria for fibromyalgia (score ≥13), indicating substantial comorbidity even though pain overall was common in the whole sample.

In the initial maintenance model, gender, race, and mental health (RAND-36) were not significant predictors of pain-related OUD maintenance, and their inclusion reduced the model's overall explanatory power to non-significance.

Mental health and pain severity (RAND-36 domains) each explained additional significant variance in PrOUD ES scores when added to the hierarchical regression model, prior to fibromyalgia's independent contribution.
Across all 46 patients, the percentage of monthly migraine days decreased significantly from baseline through 3 months of galcanezumab treatment.
